new_page.title: FHSA Explained for BC Home Buyers: $8,000 a Year, $40,000 Total
new_page.h1: How does the FHSA work when you buy a home?
new_page.description: The First Home Savings Account lets first-time buyers save $8,000 a year, $40,000 in total, with a tax deduction going in and no tax coming out.

breadcrumbs.name: How does the FHSA work when you buy a home?

faq.q: Is the FHSA better than an RRSP for a down payment?
faq.a: For a first home, usually yes: the deduction works like an RRSP but the withdrawal is not paid back. Many buyers use both.

faq.q: Can I open an FHSA if my spouse owns a home?
faq.a: Check the CRA's first-time buyer definition before you open one: it looks at homes you or your spouse or common-law partner lived in and owned in recent years.

parts.t: A First Home Savings Account (FHSA) lets a first-time buyer save up to $8,000 a year and $40,000 in total. Contributions are tax-deductible, growth is tax-free, and a qualifying withdrawal to buy your first home is not taxed. Two buyers can each have one, so a couple can bring $80,000 plus growth.

items.t: $8,000 a year, starting the year you open it
Up to $8,000 of unused room carries to the next year
Close it by December 31 of the year that comes first: the 15th anniversary of opening, the year you turn 71, or the year after your first qualifying withdrawal

parts.t: A Canadian resident aged 18 to 71 who is a first-time home buyer.

blocks.text: With the RRSP Home Buyers' Plan

parts.t: You can use your FHSA and the Home Buyers' Plan on the same purchase. Together a couple can have $80,000 of FHSA savings and $120,000 from RRSPs available for a down payment.
How the Home Buyers' Plan works.
You can move the balance to your RRSP or RRIF without tax and without using RRSP room.
Read on November 18, 2026. Rules change, so confirm with the source or your lawyer, notary or accountant before you act.
